candidates.label: Damascus (historic city center)
candidates.support: Damascus has been continuously inhabited and identified at this location since antiquity; the old city, including the street called Straight, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

summary.text: Damascus is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, capital of the Aramean kingdom in the Old Testament period and, in Acts, the city near which Paul experienced his conversion and where he first preached.

Saul arose from the ground, and when his eyes were opened, he saw no one. They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.

He took food and was strengthened. Saul stayed several days with the disciples who were at Damascus.
But Saul increased more in strength, and confounded the Jews who lived at Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.

otConnections.note: Abraham pursues the kings who captured Lot as far north as the area of Damascus.
David defeats the Arameans of Damascus and stations a garrison there.
The prophet Amos pronounces judgment on Damascus as the capital of Aram.
